function: no_learning (p. 7): BCD alternating optimization with SDR/SCA SDPs solved in CVX, closed-form power and Hungarian matching; its 'self-learning' is only an empirical quantile of CSI samples.
notes: Excluded as no_learning: every physical-layer decision comes from classical robust optimization, not from a trained model. The MUD matrix (SDR/SCA SDP) and the IRS phases (CVaR SDP) alternate by BCD, p. 7: "problem (24) is a convex SDP problem, which can be efficiently tackled by applying CVX toolboxes"; the power allocation is closed form, p. 8: "only involves a few multiplication steps and no loop structures"; the spectrum reuse is solved by the Hungarian algorithm (p. 9). The 'self-learning' of the abstract is sample-based calibration of a chance constraint: p. 7: "In order to learn the size of HPR, we collect S i.i.d. samples of the uncertain CSI", whose size is the ceil((1-delta)S)-th sorted value (eq. 30), and the CVaR uses the sample mean and covariance of the CSI (p. 7); S = 5000 (Table I, p. 10). Conclusion, p. 12: "An alternating iterative optimization algorithm was developed". No neural network, reinforcement learning, or parameter trained by minimizing a loss appears; the benchmarks are Random Reuse, Random IRS, Non-robust, and No-IRS (p. 10). If the reviewer judged this quantile calibration to be learning, the work would otherwise be area 3 (IRS phase shifts with MUD and power; SIMO uplink, M = 30, N = 40, 2 GHz, 3GPP TR 36.885 freeway with Rayleigh small-scale fading, p. 10). Identity: the PDF is arXiv:2504.11871v1 with two authors (Peng Wang, Weihua Wu); Crossref metadata of the DOI gives the same title in IEEE TVT (2026) with five authors, so it is the preprint of the same paper.
